title: ASASSN-21qj had no dust dips and no infrared excess in 2023-2026 ASAS-SN, TESS, NEOWISE and SPHEREx data; a compact 2021-2022 debris cloud needs an orbital period above 5.7 years
abstract: Question: Did the Sun-like star ASASSN-21qj recover after its 2021-2022 dust eclipse, did dips or infrared (IR) excess return up to October 2026, and which debris orbits do these data exclude? Two published models disagree: a planetary collision at 2-16 au (Kenworthy et al. 2023) and close-in exocomet dust at 0.19 au with a 30.9-day quasi-period (Marshall et al. 2023). Both used data only to 2022. Method: We calibrated ASAS-SN g photometry (to 2025-06) with 34 comparison stars, measured nine TESS sectors (2019-2026) with a spot model, averaged NEOWISE visits (2014-2024) and measured new SPHEREx 0.75-5 um fluxes (2025-04 to 2026-05) with forced PSF photometry calibrated to WISE. We shifted the observed eclipse by a period P, with optional stretch s along the orbit, and compared it with the later data. Results: After 2023-04 the g flux is 0.970 of the 2018-2020 level (season scatter 1.2%); no point is below 0.80. The non-spot TESS RMS is 1.0% in 2021, but 0.2-0.5% in 2023, 2025 and 2026, as in 2019 (0.35%). The 2018-2020 IR plateau gives f = 0.040 at 800-1000 K; it faded nearly linearly to zero near 2023-05. The 3-sigma limits at 1000 K are f < 0.0008 (NEOWISE 2023-2024) and f < 0.0044 (SPHEREx 2025-2026). A rigid repeat of the eclipse is excluded for P = 2.0-5.7 yr (a > 3.2 au for 1 solar mass); the limit is P > 4.7 yr for s = 2 and P > 3.8 yr for s = 3, and no limit for s = 5. The 2021 TESS dips give a 31.5-day correlation peak, but p = 0.14. Limitations: ASAS-SN ends in 2025-06; the TESS rule assumes that more than 10% mean dimming shows dust structure; the crowded TESS field prevents cross-sector levels; a possible 3% optical and 2% W2 deficit after 2023 is not significant. Left: the observed eclipse and two rigid repeats (P = 4.0 and 5.5 yr) that the 2023-2026 data exclude. Right: excluded debris orbital periods for stretch s and kept-dust fraction k.
TESS sectors 2019-2026: dilution-corrected flux (grey) and the residual after a spot model (blue, offset). Only the 2021 sectors show dust dips.
